paragraphs: In the morning, measure temperature and blood pressure and give medications. Change dressings, reposition patients, support respiratory hygiene, and document care. Report abnormalities at midday, communicate with families in the afternoon, monitor during rotating night shifts, and complete nursing records before handoff.

In short, they deliver foundational nursing. Work includes vital signs, medication, dressing changes, personal care, observation, and RN collaboration, combining practical skill and empathy on the frontline of care.

The greatest risk is not AI but scope boundaries plus automation. Monitoring equipment absorbs some documentation and LPN authority remains constrained by RNs, while bedside care is irreplaceable.

However intelligent equipment becomes, nurses still notice which patient seems wrong, deliver care properly, and report abnormalities. Human observation, hands, and judgment remain embedded at the bedside.
In short, the future needs licensed nurses who notice changes, deliver care well, and coordinate with RNs, not merely people who complete forms.
